note: THIS FILE IS THE OWNERSHIP MAP. ADR 005 decided it and argues for it; this file records it, and nothing else restates it. ADR 005's ownership section and CLAUDE.md's repo map point here rather than carrying a second copy, because a duplicated allowlist does not fail when it drifts. Every tracked path under `coverage.roots` must match exactly one `paths` rule: an unmatched file fails the gate, which is what makes a new directory a decision rather than a silent omission. Adding a workspace, a path rule, or a visibility class is an edit to this file alone. Schema 2 adds `publicFileSet`, which B2r moved here from a second module that had drifted 37 files away from this one.

public.summary: Ships in the public `seorak` repository under Apache-2.0.

private.summary: Stays in `seorak-internal`. The private half may depend on the public half; ADR 005 decision 1 makes every boundary-crossing arrow point private to public.

split.summary: A build input or document B4 has to divide between the two repositories. It is not yet in either set, so it is held to the public rule: an edge from here into the private tree is work B4 owes, and the gate records it rather than letting the split discover it.

mixed.summary: A workspace whose files are split across both repositories. Only a workspace identity carries this class, never a file. Nothing may import a mixed workspace by package name, because after the split no such package exists whole.

excluded.summary: Ships in NEITHER repository. ADR 005 decision 6: licensed binaries whose EULA the tree cannot evidence.

publicFileSet.note: Which tracked files land in the public repository, asked once. B2r folded a second answer, `scripts/public-file-set.mjs`, into this block: it carried its own inline rules, `public-identifiers:check` read it, and by `b5fc317` the two definitions disagreed about 37 files with both gates green. `scripts/one-public-file-set.test.mjs` fails if a third answer appears. `split` is in the set because the visibilities table already holds a split file to the public rule: its public half ships, so an identifier in it ships too, and waiting for B4 to divide the file would mean not scanning it in the meantime. C0 placed `docs/**` under `paths` and removed the `coverage.outOfScope` entry that used to stand in for a placement, so documentation is scanned like every other public file. C1b then WROTE the public half of every redaction-pending path instead of leaving them for a filter, so every `redactionPending` entry now names a PRIVATE half that does not travel, and the public half beside it at `open-core/<path>` is scanned like anything else. That is the difference between a file nobody has judged and one nobody may judge: these are the latter, and their replacements are the former.

ADR 005 decision 7 requires a trademark policy, and the wave-2 plan lists its WORDING as an owner decision with legal review, which is a gate outside engineering control. The file is placed public because that is where it lands whatever the review says; its content is marked DRAFT and carries the open questions rather than a settled policy. Apache-2.0 section 6 grants no trademark rights, so this is the only control over who may present a fork as Seorak, which is why it is a separate artifact from the licence.
